ratings_why.fun: One shared count (times played dead) feeds every payoff, and watching the Barnstormer collapse at every scratch, then take a bow, is a board you want to grow.
ratings_why.distinct: Deaths that keep the body, paid out after the fight by Curtain Calls and the critic's review, play unlike any tribe today, though Play Dead itself reads close to a familiar Reborn.

verdict_why: The flavour lands, but several cards can't be read as written (Natrix's death order, the Lead's 'shed', 'Never harmed', the Player tag); a pass on wording would fix them without changing the design.

points.text: "Your Players" reads as the person playing, on every card that names the tribe. Use the designer's own fallback, Troupers.
Dame Natrix Collar says 'a different death each time' but not which comes first. State the order (Drowned, then Poisoned, then Broken Heart) so a player can plan for it.
Milky-Eyed Juvenile Lead's 'shed' is not defined: does the Lead itself change or lose anything? Say it, or cut the word and just give the Shed Skin.
Žaltys's 'Never harmed' reads like a keyword (can't be damaged?) but does nothing. Make it flavour in italics, and say what 'smallest' means (least Attack plus Health).
Little Anguis's Tail grows between fights while not on the board. Show the Tail's size on Anguis's card ('Tail: 3/3') so the growth is visible in the shop.

standouts.why: Mr Ardea Grey: the review, rave or pan, is the seed's critic who eats actors, read straight off a visible number.
The Barnstormer: a ham who plays dead at every scratch is instantly readable and is the fantasy in one line.
Žilvinas: the Encore brings back the dead for the bow, the repertoire's twist made into a clean, dramatic rule.

weakest.why: Compost Heap Matron just hands out a Hatchling each turn; it does nothing with the tribe's deaths.
Footlights Keeper is a quiet number change with little of the stage in what it does.
The Natterjack is a generic gold-per-count card; the barker's call never shows up in play.

flags.note: With Dame Natrix's Broken Heart and Old Crest, the splash grows with the square of the deaths, held only by the cap of 10 a throw.
A rave gives every other Player up to +10/+10 a turn; worth the owner's eye once Barnstormers stack deaths.
Order of her three deaths is not stated.
'Shed' has no defined effect on the Lead.
'Never harmed' looks like a rule but isn't one; 'smallest' is undefined.
'Permanently play dead one more time each fight' is awkward; 'permanently gains one more Play Dead, up to 5' reads better.
